verbalization: Doxacurium Chloride, a quaternary ammonium salt, is closely related to Cisatracurium Besylate and Atracurium, both of which are known to bind to nicotinic acetylcholine receptors (nAChRs), specifically the α7 subunit of the nicotinic receptor (Chrna1). The evidence suggests a mechanistic link between Doxacurium Chloride and Chrna1 through a shared pathway involving quaternary ammonium salts and diester compounds. The binding of Atracurium to Chrna1 is well-documented, and since Doxacurium Chloride resembles Atracurium, it is plausible that it exerts a similar effect. The low common ancestor between Doxacurium Chloride and Atracurium indicates a shared structural feature that may contribute to its pharmacological activity. The integrated evidence supports the hypothesis that Doxacurium Chloride acts as a nicotinic receptor antagonist, potentially modulating Chrna1 function. The mechanism is supported by the structural similarity to Atracurium and the known binding of Atracurium to Chrna1, though the exact mechanism of action of Doxacurium Chloride remains to be fully elucidated.
